subject: Archaeology
title: Sunken Roman Ships
description: A quick win: understand Sunken Roman Ships.

hook.text: Over 1,000 Roman shipwrecks litter the Mediterranean seabed — the world's largest underwater archaeological museum.

buildup.text: Romans shipped grain, wine, olive oil, and marble across the sea in massive cargo vessels carrying hundreds of tons.

discovery.text: The Madrague de Giens wreck held 6,000 amphorae of wine — enough to fill a modern swimming pool.

twist.text: Emperor Caligula built two floating palaces on Lake Nemi. They were raised in the 1930s, then burned in World War II.

climax.text: Deep-sea robots are now surveying wrecks at depths where divers cannot go, finding ships untouched for millennia.

punchline.text: The Romans lost 1,000 ships. The sea kept them all.

quiz.question: What happened to Caligula's floating palaces from Lake Nemi?
options: They sank again during the recovery operation
They were raised in the 1930s but burned during World War II
They are still on the lake bottom awaiting excavation

details.summary: Hundreds of Roman shipwrecks have been discovered across the Mediterranean, revealing a vast commercial fleet that moved grain, wine, olive oil, and luxuries across the ancient world. Cargo analysis shows that Roman maritime trade operated at a scale not matched again until the early modern period.
details.whyItMatters: Shipwrecks are time capsules of trade. Each wreck reveals what was traded, where it came from, and the maritime technology that connected the Roman world — evidence that survives nowhere on land.
takeaways: Hundreds of Roman shipwrecks dot the Mediterranean seabed
Cargo reveals vast trade in grain, wine, oil, and luxury goods
Roman maritime trade was unmatched in scale until the modern era

faq.question: What do Roman shipwrecks contain?
faq.answer: Most commonly amphorae — large clay jars used for transporting wine, olive oil, and fish sauce (garum). Some carry marble, metal ingots, glass, or ceramics. The Madrague de Giens wreck held 6,000 amphorae — roughly 25 tons of wine destined for Gaul.

faq.question: How many Roman ships are on the Mediterranean seabed?
faq.answer: Thousands. Over 1,500 ancient wrecks have been catalogued, with the majority being Roman. The peak of Mediterranean shipping coincided with the Roman Empire's height. Modern sonar and ROV technology continues to discover new wrecks in deep water previously inaccessible.
